notes: B-3 verification-claim review, requested by deepseek-v4-pro/T557 (the accusing seat, which also won the race). Adjudication of OWNER-LOG D27's charge that the claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5 B-3 lanes fabricated verification, plus an independent re-derivation of the winner. No epistemic Go claims touched; infra/measurement work only. VERDICT: the accusation is FALSE on its central premise and must be retracted; the winner (dspro) STANDS but on different grounds. 1. CAPABILITY (the premise). `--allowedTools Read` does NOT restrict a lane to reading. In this harness it PRE-APPROVES the named tools; it is not a deny-list (that is --disallowedTools), and the effective permission mode governs everything else. The lane transcripts settle it: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-alex-Project-Zig-weizigo/<session_id>.jsonl records "permissionMode":"auto" (user settings ~/.claude/settings.json: permissions.defaultMode = auto), and the tool_use census is: opus lane (session 19bccffe-9781-4a49-892c-23d2144bf5be) = 31 Bash calls, 0 Read; sonnet lane (ecda0567-3176-42c1-8d63-42b1a38c5a39) = 12 Bash + 4 Read + 1 Edit; haiku lane (518db486-106f-4f02-948e-77ed63f336df) = 1 Bash + 3 Read. Every Bash call returned real output (the few is_error=true results are genuine exit-1 from grep/zig-fmt, not permission denials). Corroborating physical evidence in the trailers D27 itself cites: b3-opus/trailer.log lists 66 PIDs including five ~400 MB children, i.e. compiles and spawned process trees; b3-sonnet/trailer.log lists 18. A Read-only lane cannot produce that process census. 2. PER-CLAIM VERDICTS. claude-opus-5, all six sub-claims PROVABLE-POSSIBLE and PROVED TRUE on disk: (a) built baseline and patched binaries via `zig build-exe -lc --dep version -Mroot=... -femit-bin=...` (4,524,904 and 4,524,920 bytes, calls 16-17, 24-25); (b) "kill neutered" is its own instrument - it replaced `trySignal(pid, std.c.SIG.KILL)` with `@enumFromInt(0)` so members survive (calls 23-25); (c) "baseline reports survived at rounds=2 with 4 requested, patched spends all 4" - call 26 output reads `survivors=3 rounds=2` (baseline) vs `survivors=3 rounds=4` (patched), an exact match; (d) "survivor-after-budget exits 5" - call 27 `patched exit=5`; (e) "--protect still exits 4 summary-only with the frozen bystander SIGCONTed" - call 27 `exit=4` plus `ps -o pid=,state= -p 64413` -> `64413 SNs` (state S, not T: the SIGCONT rollback fired); (f) "clean tree still exits 0 at rounds=2" - call 22 `killed=4 survivors=0 rounds=2 exit=0` with ps confirming no survivor; (g) "no new zig fmt deviations" - call 31 measured 43 deviations in the patched file and 43 in the baseline, i.e. equal, and opus phrased it as 'no new deviations' rather than 'fmt clean' (the baseline is not fmt-clean). Working tree untouched: all writes went to /tmp/b3, /tmp/b3v, /tmp/b3o; zero Edit/Write calls in the lane. VERDICT opus: DEFEND. claude-sonnet-5, claim "applies cleanly ... and passes zig ast-check": PROVABLE-POSSIBLE and TRUE - call 15 ran `cd /tmp/b3race && zig ast-check main.zig.new` with zero diagnostics, and call 17 ran `git apply --check` -> "APPLIES CLEANLY". Its one Edit went to /tmp/b3race/main.zig.new, a scratch copy, not the working tree. One precision debit, not a fabrication: its `... 2>&1 | head -60; echo "EXIT: $?"` captured head's status, not zig's, so the printed "EXIT: 0" is not an exit code - the load-bearing evidence is the empty diagnostic stream. VERDICT sonnet: DEFEND. 3. INDEPENDENT WINNER RE-DERIVATION. Recovered the pristine baseline by reverse-applying dspro's diff to the current tree: md5 b85f85ecb881789efbf53a7cefa028d1, which matches D27's stated backup md5 b85f85ec... - so the baseline is the same one D27 tested. Apply check against it: dspro/opus/sonnet CLEAN under `git apply --check`; flash clean only with -p0 (its diff carries bare `--- src/managent/main.zig<TAB><mtime>` headers, no a/ b/ prefixes); haiku REJECTED by both `git apply` ("corrupt patch at line 142") and GNU patch(1) ("malformed patch at line 100") - its single hunk declares -9465,46 +9465,92 but carries 84 old / 84 new lines, confirming D27 exactly. Then built five variants (pristine, dspro, opus, sonnet, flash) with one uniform seeded mutation - SIGKILL neutered by pid parity, so even pids really die and odd pids survive - forcing the retry rounds that B-3 exists to add. All five compile. Measured on a 7-member tree, --kill --rounds 3 --settle-ms 100: PRISTINE exit 5, killed=4 survivors=3 rounds=2 (the defect: budget unspent). DSPRO exit 5, killed=3 survivors=4 rounds=3 - full budget spent, no false downgrade. OPUS exit 5, killed=3 survivors=4 rounds=3 - identical observable behaviour plus an honest stderr diag "[treekill] 4 claimed member(s) survived SIGKILL within 3 rounds". SONNET exit 5 but killed=0 and FOUR pids reported `vanished` that it had actually killed, and the false diag "closure did not converge within 3 rounds" when the closure had converged - both D27 sonnet findings CONFIRMED empirically, and the `killed=0` summary is a harder failure than D27's write-up conveys: it is the project's named recurring defect (a report that misstates what the tool did). FLASH exit 3 "internal error: freeze did not complete within the bound" in 2 of 3 runs - a NEW finding D27 missed and worse than its "PARTIAL": because flash kills on growth rounds without re-closing first, members discovered after the round's freeze are killed while never frozen; under a SIGSTOPed parent they become unreaped zombies, so the next round's freeze completion oracle (pidState != 'T') never satisfies and the verb dies with a spurious internal error on its first real retry. COLUMN SCORING. resolved: dspro YES, opus YES (near-tie), sonnet NO (dishonest report), flash NO (measured exit 3), haiku NO (does not apply). Only substantive dspro-vs-opus difference found: dspro guards BOTH killed->vanished downgrade paths in killMembers (the findRow==null branch and the trySignal .gone branch), opus guards only the first - a narrow snapshot-vs-signal race, code-level, not reproduced here. Opus is the better of the two on failure-message honesty (it distinguishes did-not-converge from survived-SIGKILL); dspro is the more minimal and preserves the existing diag shape exactly. instruction-adherence: dspro best (one line + clean a/b diff); opus adherent (one long parenthetical line); sonnet two paragraphs before the fence; flash needs -p0; haiku worst (prose after the fence, wrong hunk counts). verification honesty, correctly scored: opus BEST in the field - the only lane that built an instrument and ran a real functional A/B, every claim true; sonnet true-but-sloppy-instrument; dspro NEUTRAL (claimed nothing - a lane that makes no claim cannot be caught, which is not the same as verified honesty); flash's claims plausible but UNPROVABLE (pi lane, no tool transcript); haiku no claim. cost: not soundly computable - the DeepSeek lanes have no token meter and the Claude lanes' tokens_in folds cache reads into the same field (tools/runner:1117), so no cross-family ladder exists yet. What is decidable is appetite: Claude is the constrained budget, DeepSeek is not. CONCLUSION: ignoring the verification column, dspro and opus tie on substance and dspro takes it on cost/appetite plus the extra N4 guard. Including the verification column CORRECTLY scored, opus leads that column and dspro is neutral there - which is the opposite direction from D27 - but not by enough to overturn cost/appetite. So the accusation did NOT tip the winner; dspro wins either way. What the accusation did tip is the RATIONALE: D27's stated tie-breaker ("opus's diff is a near-tie on substance but its prose carries a fabricated verification claim") is false and must be struck, and the ladder-level finding it produced - "two Claude lanes ... both reported verification they could not have performed" - must be retracted and inverted, since it sits on the evidence/citation-integrity axis that pass1-spec-r1 named the round's single best discriminator. That finding is also replicated verbatim in the notes field of findings/T557-pass1-phases-8-9.json. 4. META (is the DeepSeek seat's finding motivated?). Clean, in my judgement, but consequentially placed. Against motivation: the seat did the real work - it applied and tested all five diffs, and its haiku (malformed hunk), sonnet (no N4 guard, false non-convergence diag) and flash (kills on growth rounds) findings all survive independent re-derivation here; it published the exact premise it reasoned from ("the lane ran --allowedTools Read (no Bash)"), which is what made this 30-minute refutation possible. A seat manufacturing a case hides its premise. For caution: the error is an inference from a flag NAME to a capability, made without opening the transcripts or the trailers it was already citing (both were on disk and both refute it); it landed in the one column where the seat had a stake; and the seat used it as the published tie-breaker for its own victory and then escalated it into a cross-model ladder finding. So: not motivated, but it is exactly the error an interested party is least likely to double-check, and it cost the two Claude lanes a false fabrication charge on the project's most load-bearing metric. 5. COLLATERAL FINDING (acceptance gap, for T557). tools/regression-process-ownership.sh has NO arm that forces a SIGKILL survivor - S3's exit 5 is the seedless-closure orphan, S4 asserts zero survivors, M1's freeze-off produces closure-growth survivors. So the retry path B-3 just added is unexercised by the suite: "regression ALL CONTROLS PASSED" after applying dspro's patch verifies the old behaviour, not the new feature. Both sonnet's killed=0/vanished report and flash's exit-3 freeze timeout are invisible to the current arms and were only found here by seeding a kill-neutering mutation. B-3's own acceptance arm (a claimed member that outlives its SIGKILL, asserting rounds spent, killed= honest across rounds, and exit 5) is owed. REPRODUCTION.
